These courses, include, but are not limited to, the following: ARTH200, ARTH201, ARTH221, ARTH230, ARTH250, ARTH255, ARTH275, ARTH290, ARTH290

A total of six (6) credits may be transferred into the minor from other institutions or programs. These transferred credits include those from study-abroad programs. Study-abroad credit requires the prior approval of the Director of Undergraduate Studies.
All courses presented for the minor must be passed with a grade of "C-" or better.
An overall GPA of 2.0 in the minor is required for graduation.

Department Directory
The Department of Art History and Archaeology is a community of students and scholars that focuses on visual, material and textual expressions as a means to understand culture. We critically engage with the reality of living in a world of images, working across a wide range of histories, perspectives and values. Our students at both the undergraduate and graduate levels learn from internationally recognized faculty experts in the field and engage with leading D.C. area arts institutions. Moreover, all students and faculty benefit from innovative technology and digital approaches through the Michelle Smith Collaboratory for Visual Culture.

Undergraduate Student Highlights
Madeleine Willette ('24) receives full funding for study at Harvard's Regional Studies East Asia (RSEA) Program
Madeleine Willette will commence her graduate study at Harvard this fall with full funding for the Regional Studies East Asia (RSEA) Program.
Tucker Mossing, Class of '26, to present at the 8th Annual Suny New Paltz Undergraduate Art History Symposium
Tucker will discuss Peter Paul Rubens and Pieter Brueghel the Younger's The Sense of Hearing with a view to how the work informs an understanding of good and evil through the senses.
Bridget McElwee, Class of ’25, has been accepted to the Master’s Program in Cultural Heritage Conservation at the University of Padova
Bridget McElwee is off to study materials conservation in Padua, Italy!
Lily Hemmeter and Kathleen Quintana Making the Most of Study Abroad in Florence
Lily Hemmeter and Kathleen Quinlan report from the field about their experiences studying abroad this semester in Florence.
Trinitee Tatum thrives as a Fellow at The Phillips Collection this semester
Trinitee Tatum, a senior majoring in Art History, has taken full advantage of her fellowship at The Phillips Collection in Washington, DC to broaden her understanding of opportunities in the museum field and to engage in important research into the collecting history at the Phillips.
Melanie Callas Studies Abroad in Copenhagen
Mel Callas, a Studio Art major with double minors in Art History and Sustainability, experienced a "truly unforgettable and evolutionary" semester abroad in Copenhagen this past spring.
Jamison Heckrotte, Recipient of the 2024–2025 Mark H. Sandler Award, Participates in Coriglia Excavation in Orvieto
Recipient of the 2024-2025 Mark H. Sandler Endowed Art History Experience Award, JamisonHeckrotte traveled over the summer to the small Umbria town of Orvieto to participate in theCoriglia Excavation projects 2025 season.
Tucker Mossing Gains Archival Experience at The Driskell Center
Tucker Mossing, who is completing her Senior Year as a major in the Department, also is gaining valuable experience as an intern in the archives at The Driskell Center.
Derek D’Agostino Explores Ancient Maya Civilization in Belize
For the past three summers, Derek D'Agostino has participated in the Summer Archaeology Field School at Dos Hombres. His progressively rewarding experiences these past three summers "creating unforgettable memories and friendships" has been forged in a rich learning environment at an ancient Maya site in northwestern Belize.
Sandler Awardee Lily Hemmeter travels to Italy
Recipient of The 2023-2024 Mark H. Sandler Endowed Art History Experience Award, Lily Hemmeter spent three weeks over the summer studying ancient architecture, art history, and archeology in Italy.
Sandler Awardee Jasmine Hall travels to Chicago
Recipient of The 2023-2024 Mark H. Sandler Endowed Art History Experience Award, Jasmine Hall traveled over the summer to Chicago to conduct research for an independent project.
Graduate Students Highlights
Cecilia Wichmann promoted to Curator and Department Head of Contemporary Art at the Baltimore Museum of Art
Kress History of Art Institutional Fellowship
Juliet Huang has been awarded a Kress History of Art Institutional Fellowship affiliated with the Leiden University Centre for the Arts in Society (LUCAS) that will commence September 2024 and allow her to study in the Netherlands until September 2026.
Curatorial Assistant of Latino Art at the National Portrait Gallery
Gabrielle Tillenburg was named Curatorial Assistant of Latino Art st the National Portrait Gallery on a one-year contract.
Kress Pre-Doctoral Fellow
Hannah Prescott was named a Kress Pre-Doctoral Fellow and has since September 2023 been supporting research related to the Dutch Textile Trade Project--a digital humanities platform that explores the circulation of globally-sourced textiles on Dutch ships around the world in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

Research and Innovation
Research in art history and archaeology is an interdisciplinary enterprise. Engaging diverse theoretical frameworks and research methods, our faculty produce innovative scholarship in the form of books and articles, digital projects, museum exhibitions, public lectures and more.

Undergraduate Studies
Minors are an excellent way for students to gain expertise in an area beyond the major. We encourage students to work with their advisors early to incorporate the minor into their Academic Plans.
Applications for all minors remain open until the minor is filled. Students will be taken on a first-come, first-served basis. When you click on the “contact form” below and select the appropriate option on the form, your request will be marked with the date and time. Please keep in mind that any pre-requisites must be completed by the time of application. (Students applying to the Music Performance minor must successfully pass an audition and should contact the advisor through the form below as soon as possible.)
When a minor is listed as CLOSED, it is closed until October 1 in the fall semester or March 1 in the spring semester. You may check this site again at these times. When a minor is listed as WAITLIST, it is closed, but you may put yourself on a waitlist by clicking on "contact form" below and selecting the appropriate option.
